text:
alex: heads up — after last night's runtime roll we see a 2.2x increase in per-token tail latency on /chat-stream routes (p95 -> p99). Not full outage but visible SLO risk.

maya: saw the alert, digging into the token-level waterfall. p50 steady, but p95/p99 spikes line up with small batch sizes (1-4).

jia: possible kernel selector change? the selector was tweaked to prefer the new fused-attn kernel for short sequences — could be regress for our batch distribution.

sam: I pulled telemetry. SM occupancy is high on affected hosts (~88%), VRAM utilization is ~40%, but per-MIG slice token throughput drops on the same time windows. Looks like compute-bound kernels with poor warp efficiency.

alex: here are quick queries I ran in grafana (copying for the thread):
```
sum(rate(tokens_served_total{route="/chat-stream"}[1m])) by (instance)
avg_over_time(token_latency_ms{quantile="0.99",route="/chat-stream"}[5m])
avg(smidle_utilization{mig_slice=~"slice.*"}) by (mig_slice)
```

maya: also adding panel idea: token-latency breakdown by kernel type + batch size. We need a 2D heatmap: x=batch size, y=kernel name, color=avg token-ms.

jia: quick repro: revert kernel selector to previous branch locally and run prod replay. With old selector p99 drops back to baseline. Suspect heuristics mis-routed small batches to the fused kernel which has higher per-token overhead for tiny batches.

sam: KV cache signals look noisy too — cache hit-rate dips on the same windows. Might be eviction thrash from prefetch change earlier this week. If the kernel is compute-heavier, prefetch latency + eviction could amplify tail.

alex: agreed. Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) revert kernel selector tweak 2) pin batcher min-aggregation window to 30ms for this route 3) roll a dashboard that correlates kernel -> batch size -> kv_hit_rate -> p99 token latency.

maya: I can patch dashboard panels now. Suggested panel queries: per-route kernel mix: `count_over_time(kernel_selected{route=~"/chat.*"}[5m]) by (kernel)`, kv hit heatmap: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_cache_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route))`.

infra-bot: deploy: runtime-selector-revert started by jia — build 0.85.1 -> canary 5 hosts. CI checks passed. :rocket:

jia: canary metrics look good — p99 trending down on the canary hosts after revert. Rolling to remainder over next 10m.

sam: follow-up ops item: add a MIG slice packing metric to runtime exporter. Right now we only export per-GPU SM occupancy and not per-mig-packing-efficiency; need a derived metric like `mig_fragmentation_ratio` to catch slice skew early.

alex: good call. Also want an alert rule: if p99 token latency rises by >20% AND kernel_mix[fused_attn] > 40% for 5m then page runtime-eng.

maya: I'll add dashboard mock and alert PR. Keeping panels lightweight — token waterfall, kernel mix heatmap, per-route kv hit map, per-mig sm occupancy line chart, and host-level thermal/power scatter to spot throttling.

jia: postmortem action items: 1) add A/B test harness for kernel selector changes 2) add unit tests that validate small-batch path latency 3) better metric for kv-prefetch eviction cycles.

alex: thanks all. leaving this thread open for updates while rollout finishes. If p99 doesn't return to baseline within 30m we'll revert everything.

sam: adding a short snippet of the repro script I used: 
```
# replay small-batch heavy workload against canary
python tools/replay.py --trace traces/small_batch_chat.json --target http://canary-host:8080 --concurrency 50
```

maya: PR 672 in dashboards repo created: `runtime/kernel-batch-kvcorrelate` — linking in case people want to review before the full roll.

infra-bot: deploy: runtime-selector-revert completed on 100% hosts. Roll successful. :white_check_mark:

alex: looks stable. closing thread in 1h unless objections. Great work. :trophy:
